title: Preflight randomized-failure-injection (RFI) schedule and detection runbook
body:
Purpose:
This document defines a lightweight preflight plan that injects small, randomized failures during staged rollouts to validate detection, alerting, and operator handoffs. Goal is to surface subtle telemetry gaps and ensure on-call and release-conductor playbooks catch real regressions before broad launch.

Scope and constraints:
- Applies to any feature or infra change targeting production with gradual rollout (>= 5% initial traffic).
- RFI runs are small by design: affecting a tiny percent of requests or a single region/pool.
- Legal/security: no user PII to be exposed. Avoid injecting failures into regulated customer tenants during RFI.

Quick runbook summary (for shift leads):
1) Confirm preflight checklist green: canary test pass, smoke metrics stable, schema compatibility checked.
2) Schedule RFI window in calendar and notify on-call + release channel (use template below).
3) Apply single-fault injection (see schedule) to limited scope for 10–15 minutes.
4) Observe telemetry and alerts for 30 minutes post-injection. Log observations.
5) If any SLOs degrade beyond threshold or sustained errors appear, trigger rollback decision flow.
6) Debrief and publish short findings into the release notes draft.

Randomized failure injection schedule (example matrix):
- Day 0 (canary): no RFI. Baseline only.
- Day 1, 10:00 PDT: Fault A (5% HTTP 5xx on route /generate) in single us-west pool, 10m duration.
- Day 2, 14:30 PDT: Fault B (increased token-latency tail: add 200–500ms to 3% of requests) in eu-west pool, 15m duration.
- Day 3, 09:15 PDT: Fault C (KV-cache miss storm simulated by disabling local cache for one shard) in us-east pool, 12m duration.
- Containment: each RFI targets a single pool or region and only a small traffic slice. If unexpected cascading occurs, immediate abort and rollback.

Injection knobs and safety checks:
- Feature flag control: every RFI is gated behind a feature flag with immediate kill switch (owner: release-conductor).
- Traffic percentage: cap at 5% of pool traffic; prefer 1–2% for first runs.
- Automatic abort: if error-rate > 2x normal baseline for 2 consecutive 1-minute windows, abort injection and restore config.
- Circuit breakers: ensure downstream services have small NRT timeouts to avoid queueing.

Detection responsibilities (who watches what):
- On-call SRE: watch global error-rate, service-level P95/P99 latency, throttling and queue depth dashboards.
- Release conductor: monitor route-specific metrics, feature-flag health and kill-switch responsiveness.
- Observability owner (console team): validate alert fidelity and that traces surface impacted request ids.

Telemetry and anchors to monitor:
- Error budget burn rate (per-service and per-route).
- Token-per-req latency distribution (P50/P95/P99) for generation endpoints.
- KV cache hit ratio and cache evictions.
- Queue length/backpressure metrics on worker pools.
- Traces: sampling to include injected-flagged requests. Tag injections with header X-RFI-ID.

Decision tree (short):
- If injected fault observed and metrics return to baseline within 30 minutes: mark as mitigated, note findings, continue staged rollout.
- If injected fault causes cascading failures or SLO breach persists > 30 minutes: initiate rollback and runpostmortem.
- If detection fails (we didn’t see any signal when SRE expected to): pause rollout and open an observability ticket.

Communication templates (paste into Slack release channel):
- Start message: "RFI START: injecting Fault A in us-west pool at 2026-03-10T10:00Z. Target 2% traffic. On-call @sre-team watching dashboards. Kill-switch: release-conductor.featureFlag.rfiA. RFI ID: rfi-20260310-01"
- Abort message: "RFI ABORT: observed error-rate spike in us-west. Aborting injection and rolling back config. SRE lead: Riley Chen. See runbook: <confluence link>."
- Post-run note: "RFI COMPLETE: Fault A injected for 10m. Observations: small P99 blip (250ms), no SLO breach. Action items: add trace sampling for route /generate."

Observation log template (one line per observation):
- timestamp | rfi-id | region | fault-type | immediate-metric-change | operator-action | note-link
Example: "2026-03-10T10:05Z | rfi-20260310-01 | us-west | http-5xx-5pct | error-rate +0.8% | killed flag at 10:07Z | https://confluence/observations/123"

Ownership rotation (during rollout week):
- Day shift (08:00–20:00 local): release-conductor + SRE 1 (primary) + eng-oncall (secondary).
- Night shift (20:00–08:00): SRE 2 primary, release-conductor reachable for escalations.
- Handover checklist: summary of RFI runs completed, pending items, any open alerts, link to observations log.

Rollout calendar (sample for a two-week staggered release):
- Week 1: internal canary + RFI day 1 (small, us-west).
- Week 2: regional ramp with targeted RFIs on alternating days (eu-west, ap-southeast), monitoring windows extended to 60m after each RFI.
- Week 3: global ramp if no regressions found.

Post-release notes draft (to be appended to release docs):
- Title: vX.Y.Z — preflight RFI summary and findings
- TL;DR: ran 3 short randomized-failure injections across pools to validate detection. No SLO breaches. One observation: low trace sampling prevented root-cause linking for Fault C; added immediate action item.
- What we tested: HTTP error injection, latency tail spikes, cache miss storm.
- Key findings: (1) alert threshold for cache-miss-rate needs a 10% lower sensitivity, (2) kill-switch validated within 90s, (3) trace sampling increased by +1% post-run.
- Action items: observability ticket #RFI-OBS-12, rollback guard added to runbook, follow-up test on kv-shard-3.

Publishing and follow-up:
- Publish a 1-paragraph summary to the release notes and link to the detailed observation log and postmortem if an incident is triggered.
- Track action items in Linear and tag eng-sre and console teams.

Notes and open questions (for the next iteration):
- How to simulate token-quota exhaustion without risking customer throttles? Proposal: use synthetic tenant in staging mirrored to prod-like infra.
- Should RFIs be run automatically as part of CI for infra changes? Risk: noisy false-positives for small deploys.

Appendix: quick links and knobs:
- Kill-switch playbook: confluence:release/kill-switchs
- Feature-flag console: https://flags.redwood.internal
- Observability dashboards: https://console.redwood.internal/dashboards/rfi-core

End of runbook - keep this doc near the release-conductor binder and update after each RFI iteration.
